A key assumption made in the direct collocation method for optimal control is the ability to represent the state dynamics and control inputs through a finite-dimensional approximation, typically achieved by discretizing the control inputs and the state trajectory over a finite time horizon. This approach entails the assumption that the continuous-time optimal control problem can be accurately approximated by a discrete set of control inputs, which are evaluated at specific collocation points within the discretized time intervals.
